description.narrative:

Outcome 2: Women¿s participation and leadership in decision-making in the public and private sectors is promoted, and women and girls benefit from gender-responsive governance.

description.narrative: SDG 5.2.1. https://unstats.un.org/sdgs/indicators/databaseCustodian(s): UNICEF, UN Women, UNFPA, WHO, UNODCThis is a Tier II indicator (as of May 2021). Please check data availability for your country of interest.Note: Due to constraints related to feasibility, this indicator currently globally reports only on the percentage of everpartnered women and girls aged 15 to 49 who have experienced physical and/or sexual partner violence.For more information on the methodology, refer to the SDG Indicators Metadata repository https://unstats.un.org/sdgs/metadata/

comment.narrative: Tanzania DHS 20152016 Experience of violence from anyone Forty percent of women aged 1549 have ever experienced physical violence and 17 have ever experienced sexual violence. Although the experience of violence is higher among married women particularly formerly married women 16 of nevermarried women have also ever experienced physical violence and 9 have ever experienced sexual violence. Marital control Nearly three quarters of evermarried women experienced marital control by their husbandspartners including 29 whose husbandpartner demonstrated at least three of the five specified behaviors. Spousal violence Half of all evermarried women have ever experienced spousal violence most commonly physical violence 39 and emotional violence 36 14 have experienced sexual violence.There is no current national data on VAW prevalence in Tanzania and Zanzibar. TDHS of 201516 issued the last VAW data. The government is finalizing the national data on VAW prevalence to be published in the last quarter of 2023.
Estimate target. Value will be updated after the release of the new TDHS Survey

title.narrative: Indicator 2.1.1: Number of women leaders demonstrating increased capacity on leadership and gender mainstreaming.

description.narrative: The indicator is designed to measure the development and growth of women leaders skills and knowledge in the areas of leadership and gender mainstreaming. Data for this indicator will be counted as follows:Identification of Women Leaders: Identify and document the women who are in leadership positions within the project or relevant institutions. These women may hold positions such as managers, supervisors, team leaders, or any other roles with leadership responsibilities.Capacity Building Programs: Implement capacitybuilding programs or initiatives that focus on leadership skills and gender mainstreaming. These programs may include training workshops, mentoring, coaching, or educational courses.PreAssessment: Conduct an initial assessment to evaluate the participants knowledge and skills related to leadership and gender mainstreaming before they undergo the capacitybuilding programs.Training and Development: Provide training and development opportunities to the women leaders, ensuring that they gain a deeper understanding of leadership principles and gender mainstreaming concepts.PostAssessment: After the capacitybuilding programs, conduct a postassessment to measure the increase in the participants capacity in leadership and gender mainstreaming.Counting: The count will be based on the number of women leaders who demonstrate increased capacity in leadership and gender mainstreaming, as evidenced by improvements in their knowledge, skills, and application of these principles.This indicator is essential for tracking the impact of capacitybuilding initiatives in enhancing the leadership abilities of women and promoting gender mainstreaming within organizations and communities. It demonstrates the projects commitment to empowering women in leadership roles while advancing gender equality and inclusion.

title.narrative: Indicator 2.1.2: Status of womens participation in leadership and decisionmaking roles in select public institutions

description.narrative: The indicator aims to assess and track the representation and involvement of women in key leadership and decisionmaking positions within specific public institutions. Data for this indicator will be counted as follows:Identification of Public Institutions: Begin by identifying and selecting the specific public institutions that will be included in the assessment. These institutions may include government bodies, agencies, local councils, or other relevant organizations.Data Collection: Collect data on the current status of womens participation in leadership and decisionmaking roles within the selected institutions. This data may include the number of women holding leadership positions, their roles, and their levels of authority or decisionmaking influence.Define Key Metrics: Establish key metrics or criteria to evaluate the level of womens participation and their decisionmaking roles. These criteria may involve seniority, leadership titles, the scope of responsibilities, or other relevant factors.Data Analysis: Analyze the collected data to determine the extent of womens participation and decisionmaking authority within the selected public institutions.Counting: The count will be based on the number of women who hold significant leadership and decisionmaking roles as defined by the established metrics within the selected institutions. The count may be expressed as a percentage or an absolute number, depending on the projects goals and reporting format.This indicator is vital for tracking progress in promoting gender diversity and womens empowerment in public institutions, providing insights into the extent of womens participation in shaping policies and decisions within these organizations.
